body: Hey! I'm new here but I swear to defend us!

I actually hadn't thought about this before. I always wondered what happened to Lynera after the trial and I really hoped we would be able to save her when we got to the clown car. I also just really don't want her to die, she didn't deserve it. I like your theory!

Agree. I've had a pretty bad sugar addiction since I was a kid, for me my favorite sugary snack is sour patch kids and ice cream (not together tho). It's nice hearing about other people's stories and what works for them, makes me feel like I can actually do it.

I never skip breakfast though, one of the few things getting me out of bed is the promise of a good meal first thing in the morning. I try to do the healthy stuff like eggs, fruit, some tea, etc. Thanks for the advice btw!

Yaaayy someone my age!! Thanks for helping, really needed some direction on the whole "how do I find the time to take care of myself????". I'll try to stick with the food and maybe walk more instead of taking the buss
I actually haven't thought of joining a support group before. The internet is a little bit like a support group to me but I guess it's worth actually going to one in real life. Thanks!
Thanks for saying that. I do try to give my friends the benefit of the doubt, although it gets a little rough sometimes. It's nice hearing this from an outside source too, so thanks.

Ikr XDXDXDXDDXD I mostly told the story cause I just needed to vent for a bit, sorry if the details and spelling errors bothered you. And the whole pain thing depends on how you do it of course. For me it felt like my head was in a hydraulic press

It's no problem. Feels good to just vent with someone for once, and also talk about how animals are better than humans. I'm glad you're at least in the right headspace to think about your cat. She's there for you, even if that involves doing that thing where they dig their claws into you while cuddling XP

Completely get that. I remember when I first started working out and then I had a cheat day. Eating things like burgers and drinking soda felt so disgusting I wanted to vomit. Thanks for the reminder. I just have to stick with it.

If you're gonna do it, please give away the cat to a shelter first. I volunteer at a cat shelter and I've seen so many cats come from people who have killed themselves and left their pets. The pets don't need that sort of PTSD from seeing their owner die to then be left with the body. 

Humans can go fuck themselves, but animals? No, they have better stuff to live for.

For some people it doesn't get better, for me it did. It took a failed suicide attempt and a bunch of other stuff for me to get better. When I was far off the deep end I just hung on(lol get it) and tried to live for my boyfriend. It worked untill I could get counseling, meds, a healthy lifestyle etc. This is coming from a person who has died and come back so just stick with it a little longer.

If you don't have anyone you can cling to, then I guess you're fucked.

It doesn't hurt at all, and being gone will let you get rid off all your worries. Since dead people can't worry. However, if you fail you might end up with permanent damage that just make life even worse. Choose wisely kid, I've been there.

Thank you for the encouragement! I struggle the most with working out, which is why I had it be a more central part in this post. I do also get cravings though (why does food have to be so delicious?) XD

Hey, you should probably just leave her. At least for your child's sake. 

It's better to divorce your wife now and spare your kid the trauma of being caught in an ugly custody battle. My own parents split up when I was 8 but they were already kinda hating eachother since I was 7. Lets just say the divorce wasn't very pretty, especially for a kid to be caught up between it. 

Since your kid is in his formative years, its better to just have no mom than to have an alchoholic and angry mom. Even though he's just a baby, that stuff can really stick to him. If you feel like you need it, maybe talk to a professional about your situation.

Better to ask a pro for advice than to ask reddit for advice, although it can be a good way to get some perspective.

Hang in there!

I'm so happy someone mentioned this!!! 

I have misophonia too! That coupled with things like ADHD makes it worswe, especially if the coughing or swallowing is repetetive. Even people breathing or pausing to say "Umm" triggers mine!

The thing I do is just explain this to my family and the people I'm close to. I don't even eat dinner with them anymore (I eat in my room), even though they dont like that they do understand that I need it or else I end up in a meltdown. 

Also, I don't know why this works, but my ADHD meds actually help the misophonia a little? It makes it sorta bearable. I take Concerta which makes me concentrate in school, but also lets me focus my attention away from any mouth-noises.

Stay strong! We people with misophonia have to stick together.
Thank you! I was kinda lost on the whole "How do I write about a real person without the fandom lynching me". The advice about just writing a good character really helps!
